confirmed.title: 156 of 205 exported pages share the identical <title> "German Learning OS"
confirmed.evidence: Scanned every <title> in the export: 50 distinct values across 205 pages. "German Learning OS" is used verbatim by 156 pages — every lesson, every activity, all six hubs, all 69 vocabulary details, all 10 verb details, all 10 grammar details, all 64 phrase entries, /search, /review, /review/session/today, /practice and its 7 game routes, /conversation, /settings, /references, /404.html and /_not-found. The only unique titles are the 48 professions rows plus /collections/professions. The same 156 pages also share one identical meta description. Source confirms the cause: `export const metadata` / `generateMetadata` exists in exactly three files — app/layout.tsx:6, app/collections/professions/page.tsx:6, app/collections/professions/[sourceRow]/page.tsx:19 — so every other route inherits the root layout title unchanged.
confirmed.consequence: A screen-reader learner navigating from /vocabulary/id-…lehrer to /vocabulary/id-…arzt hears "German Learning OS" both times — the title, which is the first thing announced on route change and the primary orientation cue, never tells them where they are. Sighted learners with several tabs open, and anyone using browser history or bookmarks, get 156 indistinguishable entries. WCAG 2.4.2 Page Titled is Level A, and it fails on 76% of routes.
confirmed.location: E:\claude-cursor\side projects\German learning\platform\apps\web\app\layout.tsx:6 (sole title source for 156 routes); observable at platform\apps\web\out\lessons\01\index.html, out\vocabulary\id-6c65783a6c6568726572\index.html, out\search\index.html, out\settings\index.html, out\404.html
confirmed.suggestedFix: Add `generateMetadata` to each dynamic route segment (lessons/[lessonSegment], .../activity/[activityId], vocabulary|verbs|grammar|phrases/[entityId], conversation/[entityId]) returning the entity's learner-facing label, and `export const metadata` to each static route (hubs, listening, concepts, search, review, practice + game routes, conversation, settings, references, not-found). Reuse the existing centralized lesson-label formatter so the title matches the visible h1. Title template `"%s | German Learning OS"` on the root layout keeps the product name.

confirmed.title: Practice and activity feedback is announced at most once — the live region is created with its message, and repeated identical outcomes produce no DOM change at all
confirmed.evidence:
Two compounding defects in the same channel. (1) Every feedback live region is mounted together with its content rather than existing beforehand: `{feedback ?

{feedback}

: null}` — nine such conditional live regions across components (ActivityInteraction.tsx:248,335,336; ConversationLadder.tsx:158; GameRenderer.tsx:107; DetailLearningControls.tsx:130; SettingsView.tsx:69; ReviewViews.tsx:190,191) plus four components that `return null` until there is a message (GameFeedback.tsx:17-23, ConversationFeedback.tsx:16-24, QaPractice.tsx:49 and :101, VerbSelfCheck.tsx:86). GameFeedback is the sole feedback channel for all six enabled practice games. (2) The messages are fixed constant strings — lib/games/game-grading.ts:53 "That answer could not be checked safely…", :65 "Enter or select an answer before submitting.", :79 "Matches the published form…", :90 "Matches after hint or reveal…", :100 "Does not match the published form. You can retry or reveal."; ActivityInteraction.tsx sets "Not yet. Check the words from this lesson and try again." for every wrong answer. Setting React state to a value it already holds is a no-op: no re-render, no text-node mutation, no live-region event.
confirmed.consequence: A blind learner playing Article choice, Word order, Verb builder, Morphology puzzle or Picture–word match submits a wrong answer and (if the first mount announces at all) hears "Does not match the published form." They try a different wrong answer and hear nothing — the message string is identical, so the DOM never changes. Silence is indistinguishable from a broken button, so the learner cannot tell whether their second attempt was wrong, was correct, or was never registered. The same holds in every lesson activity: the second and every subsequent wrong answer to "Check answer" is silent. This is the core learn-attempt-feedback loop of the product.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Render the feedback region unconditionally (empty text when idle) so it exists before the first message, and give each announcement a distinct identity so repeats still fire — e.g. hold `{text, seq}` in state and bump `seq` on every submission, keying the message node on `seq`, or append an attempt counter to the announced string. Do not rely on message-string inequality.

confirmed.title: 321 operable controls on 122 pages have an accessible name that does not contain their visible label — every audio control in the app
confirmed.evidence: Compared each control's aria-label against its own visible text (aria-hidden descendants removed) across all 205 pages: 321 operable failures on 122 pages, plus 196 more on disabled controls. Two patterns dominate. 188 meaning-plate buttons on 72 pages read `` — visible label "Listen", accessible name "Play der Lehrer pronunciation", which does not contain "Listen" at all. 124 primary buttons on 116 pages read `` — the accessible name splits the visible string "Play pronunciation" around the lemma, so it is not contained contiguously. Worst pages: /vocabulary (69), /phrases (37), /grammar (10), /practice (8). Also /hubs `Search all content`. A further 196 disabled buttons show "Pronunciation unavailable" while named "der Elektriker unavailable" (55 profession pages).
confirmed.consequence: A learner using Dragon, Voice Control or Voice Access — including anyone with a motor impairment who drives the app by speech — looks at a vocabulary card, says "click Listen", and nothing happens, because the speech engine matches against the accessible name. Every single pronunciation control in the app is unreachable by voice, on the hub pages (69 on /vocabulary alone) and on every detail page. Pronunciation playback is the primary interaction of a language-learning app.
confirmed.location: E:\claude-cursor\side projects\German learning\platform\apps\web\out\vocabulary\index.html (69 instances), out\phrases\index.html (37), out\vocabulary\id-6c65783a6c6568726572\index.html; rendered by components\audio\PronunciationControl.tsx and the meaning-plate audio button
confirmed.suggestedFix: Make the accessible name start with the visible label. Change the meaning-plate button to `aria-label="Listen — der Lehrer pronunciation"` (or drop aria-label and add a visually-hidden lemma span inside the button), and the primary control to `aria-label="Play pronunciation — der Friseur"`. Same treatment for the disabled variant ("Pronunciation unavailable — der Elektriker") and the /hubs link.

confirmed.title: German the learner must read or produce is left in the English language context inside 50 interactive controls, plus 25 prose spans
confirmed.evidence: The app marks German thoroughly overall (3,227 lang="de" elements) but misses it exactly where the German is the exercise. 34
confirmed.consequence: A screen-reader learner doing the verb self-check on /verbs/id-…arbeiten opens the Person dropdown and hears the seven German pronouns rendered by an English voice — "ich" as "itch", "ihr" as "ear", "sie" as "sigh". Those pronouns are the entire content being taught on that page. The same happens on the word-order builders, where the learner is choosing between German tokens spoken in English phonics. The app actively teaches the wrong pronunciation to the learners who most depend on synthesized speech.
confirmed.location: E:\claude-cursor\side projects\German learning\platform\apps\web\components\details\VerbSelfCheck.tsx (select/options; visible in out\verbs\id-766572623a617262656974656e\index.html); components\activities\ActivityInteraction.tsx:92-106 (token bank) and :139 (typing input); out\grammar\id-6772616d3a70726573656e742d636f6e6a75676174696f6e2d6c31\index.html (prose)
confirmed.suggestedFix: Put lang="de" on the <select> (it inherits to all options), on each .activity-token button, and on the typing input — matching what QaPractice.tsx:35 and the builder's <strong lang="de"> already do. For mixed-language prose, wrap the German terms in <span lang="de"> as the footer credit already does for "Momente".

confirmed.title: All 8 practice-selection cards use aria-label that replaces, rather than supplements, their visible description and status
confirmed.evidence: On /practice each card is `FlashcardsRate how well you remember each word.Enabled`. The aria-label wins the name computation, so the description and the availability chip are discarded from the accessible name for 6 of the 7 game cards plus the conversation card (which shows "Conversation ladder / Model → recognition → substitution → construction → spoken role-play / 5 levels" but is named only "Conversation practice" — the name does not even contain the visible title "Conversation ladder"). Only the audio-match card preserves its state, via aria-label="Audio match (unavailable)".
confirmed.consequence: A screen-reader learner tabbing the practice menu hears seven bare game names with no indication of what any of them does, and — except for audio-match — no indication of which are enabled. The visible "Enabled" / "Unavailable" chips that tell sighted learners which modes are ready are not in the name. On the conversation card, speech-input users saying "click Conversation ladder" (the visible title) get no match.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Drop aria-label from the cards and let the visible spans compute the name, or extend it to include what is being hidden — `aria-label="Flashcards — Rate how well you remember each word. Enabled"`. For the conversation card use the visible title "Conversation ladder" as the name stem. Prefer conveying availability with aria-disabled plus visible text rather than only a chip.

confirmed.title: The Q&A construction text field on 15 phrase pages is named "Type an answer pattern" while its visible label reads "Your answer pattern"
confirmed.evidence: On all 15 /phrases/id-… detail pages: ``. A correct programmatic label is already present via label[for], and the aria-label then overrides it with different wording. The accessible name "Type an answer pattern" does not contain the visible label "Your answer pattern".
confirmed.consequence: A learner using speech input on a phrase page says "click Your answer pattern" — the visible words next to the box — and nothing is focused. A screen-reader learner comparing what a sighted helper reads out ("Your answer pattern") with what they hear ("Type an answer pattern") gets two different names for the same field.
confirmed.location: E:\claude-cursor\side projects\German learning\platform\apps\web\components\details\QaPractice.tsx:30-42; visible in out\phrases\id-71613a6964656e74697479\index.html and 14 sibling phrase pages
confirmed.suggestedFix: Remove the aria-label from the input; the existing `<label for="qa-construction-input">` with its "Your answer pattern" span already provides a correct and matching accessible name.

confirmed.title: Gender badge text (der/die/das · Masculine/Feminine/Neuter) is 3.13–4.10:1 — the product's core semantic label fails AA on 53 routes
confirmed.evidence: `.gender-badge--masculine/feminine/neuter` (globals.css:1615-1631) set `color: var(--gender-*)` raw over `background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--gender-*) 8%, white)`. Measured from live computed styles at 13px / weight 650 (normal text, needs 4.5): masculine #246bfd on #edf3ff = 4.10; feminine #e64c86 on #fdf1f5 = 3.32; neuter #2e9d68 on #eef7f3 = 3.13. Confirmed on .gender-badge__token, .gender-badge__label and the .german article text inside the badge, across /vocabulary/, /practice/picture-word-match/, /lessons/02/activity/…636f72652d70726f66657373696f6e73/ and the noun-system panels. 53 routes contain .gender-badge. The same stylesheet already solves this correctly one level away: `.visual-cue[data-tone=…]` (globals.css:288-330) uses hand-darkened inks (#174dac, #a92f5d, #1f744d) over the same 9% tints and measures 5.2–6.9:1.
confirmed.consequence: The gender cue is the single most-repeated piece of teaching in the product, and on tinted plates its label sits below AA — hardest hit is neuter/feminine, exactly the genders learners confuse most. In sunlight or on a low-quality phone panel the pink and green labels wash out.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Introduce --gender-m-ink / --gender-f-ink / --gender-n-ink darkened variants (the .visual-cue tones #174dac / #a92f5d / #1f744d already measure 5.2–6.9:1 on these grounds) and use them for `color:` while keeping --gender-* for the swatch fill and border, so the shape glyph keeps its identifying hue.
